data.source: AMIS belt median via Kissan Cares

data.title: AMIS maize 23 Nov: belt median steady at Rs6,431 per 100 kg on eight mandis; other Punjab median falls to Rs7,375
data.summary: Belt median Rs6,431 per 100 kg (Rs2,572 per 40 kg) on 23 Nov across eight mandis with Kamalia (Rs6,875) now reporting, versus Rs6,438 on 22 Nov; Sahiwal still lowest at Rs4,650 and Arifwala eased to Rs6,425. Other Punjab mandis fell 3.3% to a Rs7,375 median as Sargodha, Lodhran and DG Khan joined.

data.title: TCP floats third tender for 800,000 t of imported wheat as flour keeps rising
data.summary: The government plans another 800,000 t of wheat imports; TCP's tender closes 30 Nov with delivery to Karachi or Gwadar by 15 Feb 2027, and officials say 550,000 t is already contracted.

data.title: Karachi fine flour up Rs20 to Rs210/kg despite fifth Romanian wheat cargo
data.summary: MV Alex brought 54,983 t of Romanian wheat to Port Qasim on 23 Nov, taking TCP imports to 273,603 t on five ships; Karachi millers still raised fine flour Rs20 to Rs210/kg and No. 2.5 flour Rs15 to Rs190/kg, with open-market wheat at Rs150/kg.

data.title: Punjab cane growers demand Rs700 a maund as most mills still defy the crushing order
data.summary: PMML is demanding Rs700 per 40 kg for cane against Rs350–475 reportedly paid; only one of Punjab's 47 mills was crushing regularly by 18 Nov, with about 1.1 Mt of surplus sugar still in warehouses.

data.act: Keep buying dry new-crop in weekly lots, starting with Sahiwal (Rs46.5/kg for a third report, check moisture on such a low price), then Pakpattan (Rs63.5/kg), Vehari (Rs63.8/kg), Arifwala (Rs64.3/kg) and Mailsi (Rs64.4/kg); Okara is Rs74.8/kg and Kamalia Rs68.8/kg. Reject lots above 14% moisture or failing aflatoxin.
data.why: The belt median held at Rs64.3/kg on 23 Nov (eight mandis, Kamalia added) against Rs64.4/kg on 22 Nov; it is 0.6% above 23 Oct (Rs63.9/kg), 15.7% below a year ago (Rs76.3/kg on 23 Nov 2025) and at 35% of its 52-week range (Rs54.4–82.5/kg). Other Punjab mandis fell to Rs73.8/kg, but the belt stays the cheapest source as autumn-crop arrivals peak in Nov–Dec.

data.act: Cover winter wanda needs for 30–45 days now with quotes from two flour mills; flour is rising faster than wheat, so mills will push bran prices up next.
data.why: AMIS Punjab wheat median is Rs125.0/kg on 23 Nov (13 mandis), 19% above 1 Sep, and flour keeps climbing: Karachi fine flour rose Rs20 to Rs210/kg on 23 Nov even as a fifth Romanian cargo arrived, after PBS showed flour +4.42% to Rs3,100 per 20 kg bag in the week to 19 Nov. TCP's third 800,000 t import tender (closing 30 Nov, delivery by 15 Feb) shows supply stays tight, and bran tightens through winter until the April harvest.

data.refreshNote: Maize 23 Nov added (belt median Rs6,431 per 100 kg on eight mandis, other Punjab Rs7,375), four intel items on wheat imports, Karachi flour and the cane-price dispute, and the maize and wheat-bran views refreshed; CBOT's 23 Nov close was not available (Brownfield failed to load, Pro Farmer not yet posted), wheat is still 23 Nov, rice rows are generic paddy, and USD/PKR and PBS urea have no newer figure.
